title: Install or configure Cast discovery
summary: Install the Cast CLI and matching provider bundle, initialize private state, inspect readiness and budgets, change collection configuration, or reconcile retained employer ownership.
use_when: Cast should be installed, initialized, diagnosed or explicitly reconfigured.
The caller needs to inspect local budgets or determine why configured sources are unavailable.
Existing ATS or older JSON-LD records need the supported employer-ownership correction without resetting paid usage.
do_not_use_when: A current discovery run or a read-only employer/job export is the requested outcome.
A schedule, provider subscription purchase, credential change, database deletion or downstream action is intended.
outcome: An installed matching program/documentation release, initialized Cast state, supported diagnostic result, explicitly replaced configuration or transactionally reconciled employer ownership.
effects: Deployment stages a content-addressed wrapper, Rust payload, Rust installer and exact provider bundle and advances only Cast-owned command/provider selectors. It creates no collection database or schedule.
Init creates private local state. Explicit configuration changes affect subsequent collection; diagnostic reads do not start paid searches.
The installed wrapper sources ~/.zshrc with output suppressed and starts the Rust payload with only the documented environment and two provider keys.

Source add retains an explicit source. Ordinary websites may use an existing company ID or a hostname candidate; supported ATS URLs use their canonical provider/tenant owner and reject --company-id. Source disable preserves evidence but removes that source from ordinary collection.

Ownership reconciliation applies current adapter rules to stored ATS source/job associations, sets older or shared-host JSON-LD jobs to unknown, restores affected search-candidate names and clears shared-host company domains, website URLs and aliases. It preserves source/job IDs, source metadata, paid request accounting, run history and query checkpoints.
authority: Cast owns its installation, state schema, configuration validation and local allowance accounting.
The caller chooses collection policy and provider accounts; provider balances are managed by each provider.
success: Installation switches command and matching documentation coherently and passes version/help checks.
Initialization, configuration or diagnosis returns its documented outcome without claiming that an external collection succeeded.

Ownership repair returns moved_sources, moved_jobs, quarantined_jobs, renamed_candidates and cleared_shared_identities counts after one committed transaction; changed jobs/companies retain identity and gain material revisions.
failure_and_recovery: Deployment refuses foreign selectors and mismatched provider/candidate versions; a failed switch restores prior Cast selectors.
Program rollback does not restore domain state. Preserve the state directory consistently before any database recovery, and do not hand-edit database rows.
Resolve missing keys or provider restrictions separately; configuration changes do not purchase credits or reset accumulated usage.
privacy: Keys remain in the caller environment and user-owned shell configuration, outside the Cast database and installed provider bundle.
State and exports may reveal personal search interests and should remain private.
does_not_authorize: Selecting jobs for the user, creating CRM cases or application packets, sending email, submitting applications, invoking an agent or browser, or enabling a schedule.
Changing provider billing, automatic purchases, another product installation, or deleting retained state.

consumers.statement: The current user may install Cast, initialize selected state, inspect configuration/readiness, explicitly change collection policy and invoke the supported ownership repair.

preconditions.statement: Installation requires a tested executable candidate matching provider release, user-owned paths and available macOS shell tools. State operations require the appropriate valid selected directory and configuration.

inputs.statement: The Rust installer install command accepts --binary and --bundle at absolute paths, plus optional --home and --expected-current. Its recover command accepts --release at a canonical owned release directory. The CLI accepts --state-dir and explicit init, configuration, diagnostic or state reconcile-ownership commands. Ordinary website source controls accept an optional company ID; supported ATS sources reject that override and use their canonical tenant owner.

outputs.statement: Deployment exposes matching Cast command and provider selectors. State commands return configuration, readiness, budget information or ownership-repair counts without exposing keys.

data_semantics.statement: Deployment readiness is program integrity, not provider authentication or collection success. Local budgets are conservative Cast counters, not authoritative provider invoices.

identity_and_units.statement: Release identity hashes program, frontend, Rust installer and provider bytes. Provider release and database/config/export schemas remain separate; request-budget units are defined by Cast configuration.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Configuration and diagnostic reads reflect selected local state. External credentials and provider allowances require their own actual provider interactions.
No current provider balance or successful network-collection guarantee follows from installation or local diagnosis.

access.statement: Installed command is ~/.local/bin/cast; immutable releases are beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Cast/install. Discovery state defaults to ~/.local/share/cast and may be selected explicitly. The wrapper reads THEIRSTACK_API_KEY and BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY from ~/.zshrc.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Deployment uses product/catalog locks and atomic current selection with coherent program/provider rollback. Initialization, collection and ownership reconciliation are separate explicit operations. Reconciliation holds one mutation lock and transaction; repeated repair is materially idempotent, while every invocation advances the snapshot revision.

operational_limits.statement: Installation creates no daemon, LaunchAgent, scheduler binding, model job or remote-provider request. No live-state migration is performed by the Rust installer.
No future migration or deployment-latency service level is promised.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability version 1 publishes Cast 0.1 installation and state-operation boundaries. Incompatible state changes require an explicit recovery and migration design.

reliances.statement: Installed credential loading relies on the user-owned ~/.zshrc executed by zsh; Chancery documents but does not execute or validate that shell configuration.
